rows.title: Policy divergence
rows.read: CPI broke the October hold: September core beat twice (0.3% m/m, 2.6% y/y) and October 27–28 went from ~23% to a coin flip (~43–54% across afternoon snapshots); December effectively fully priced (>95% odds of at least one hike by year-end). Yields spiked then faded: 2Y to ~4.95%, settled 4.80% on 3pm ET values; 10Y touched 5.33%, settled ~5.27%. The afternoon confirmed the hawkish read — the Beige Book ran hot-leaning (3 districts ‘robust,’ oil ‘permeated all District reports’) and Goolsbee called the print ‘discouraging.’ ECB: October ~12%, December the live meeting; BoJ: October ~9%, December >80% (‘December, not October’); BoE Nov 5 ~86%; RBA Nov 2–3; BoC/RBNZ Oct 28.

rows.title: Growth differentials
rows.read: Comparative growth stands where the morning left it: the US 29k payrolls shock vs AI-boom demand; the UK's Thursday 1:00am CT data dump (GDP fcst -0.1% m/m) is the next growth-vs-hike test; China's export boom (+36.3%) is export-led, not a domestic breakout (CPI 0.9%). No new growth print moved a currency today — CPI owned the tape.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.read: The pillar of the day. September CPI: headline 3.7% y/y (vs 3.6% est) on +0.6% m/m; core 0.3% m/m (vs 0.2%) and 2.6% y/y (vs 2.5%) — beats on both core measures, so pressure is broadening past energy (gasoline +9.1% was over half the monthly gain, but shelter +0.4% and services ran hot too). Pipeline: German WPI +8.7% y/y (hottest since Feb 2023); China PPI +5.0% y/y (fastest since June 2022) on oil. The Fed's own Beige Book confirmed it — ‘higher oil prices permeated all District reports.’ What matters is what the bank does about it: October is live again.

rows.title: Risk sentiment
rows.read: Risk kept expressing through crude, not currencies. The post-CPI dollar bid was a rate repricing, not a fear bid — and it partially faded into the close (2Y 4.95% → 4.80%, EUR/USD 1.1127 → 1.1157). The yen was the day's holdout: USD/JPY round-tripped the whole CPI spike to close flat. The franc kept sleeping. AUD's $0.70 test failed; NZD hovers near its 52-week low. Silver's -3% to -6% was the cleanest risk-off tell.

rows.title: Terms of trade / commodities
rows.read: Oil held the re-bid: Brent ~$106.56 (+0.6%), WTI ~$95.66 (+1.5%), spread ~$10.9 — the Aramco-building confirmation and two confirmed Hormuz vessel strikes (one sunk) kept the shipping premium bid; OPEC cut 2026 demand growth a sixth straight time (to ~180k bpd) while lifting 2027. The crude tax on JPY/EUR importers persists; the tailwind for CAD fully offset the Fed repricing today (USD/CAD flat). Gold slid toward ~$4,080 (-2%) as the rate leg beat the dollar leg.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.read: The crowd got paid. Friday's COT had USD aggregate longs ~$35.5bn (+$8.9bn WoW) crowded into CPI — the hot print rewarded them; the unwind risk now flips to the other side (a soft PPI would hurt). EUR shorts (-99,332, ~0th pctile) and AUD shorts (-98,588, record gross) also profited — the squeeze setups are still loaded but denied their trigger. Contrarian rule unchanged: stretched longs = unwind risk, stretched shorts = squeeze potential. Next COT Friday.

rows.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk
rows.read: France cleared a first hurdle — the Socialist rejection motion failed 236–149 — but the debt fight moves to the revenue vote Oct 20 and Moody's Oct 23; Lagarde: the solution ‘lies at home in France.’ Germany's 30y auction held at 3.8% — steady absorption, no duration fear. No new US fiscal development.
